subject.title: feat(onboarding): offer detected Claude Code/Codex/Hermes memory imports across CLI, macOS, and Linux onboarding

question: Should this onboarding feature wait until the observed migration-backup hang is bounded or fixed, or may it ship while that existing risk remains reachable from first-run onboarding?
rationale: The branch intentionally exposes an existing apply path in a more prominent first-run workflow, and its own Linux E2E encountered an indefinite backup stall; accepting that exposure is a maintainer-owned availability decision.

options.title: Bound import before merge
options.body: Add a safe cancellation or timeout path, or land the backup exclusion fix first, then prove onboarding can recover without restarting the application.

options.title: Accept the existing apply risk
options.body: Merge with the known possibility that selecting Import can stall onboarding, and track the backup defect as an urgent follow-up.

options.title: Narrow the initial rollout
options.body: Land the proven CLI flow first and defer native onboarding surfaces until successful end-to-end completion evidence is available.

recommendation.title: Bound import before merge
recommendation.body: Add a safe cancellation or timeout path, or land the backup exclusion fix first, then prove onboarding can recover without restarting the application.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is coordinating the cross-surface implementation and is the strongest available owner for deciding whether the known migration availability risk is acceptable.
